body: Yes. Experiencing this issue as well.
Needs test coverage in addition to a fix. The current test suite is passing.

I've pushed a fix for this problem, and added an isolated test case for it. However I'm going to leave this issue open. This should have never passed CI and I consider our lack of integration test coverage a bug. We need to make sure that we have the tests required to prevent this from happening in the future.

Thank you, Sean, for looking into this! However, with `has_many` associations the issue still remains.

Hash or Array expected, got ActionController::Parameters

issue.title: We need better integration test coverage
issue.body:
There's a serious gap in our test coverage, in places that our gems interface with each other. https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/20922 for example, should never have happened. It looks like at the moment the closest thing we have to integration tests are the railties tests, but that is insufficient. I'd like to propose that we introduce an additional test suite that involves running unit tests for a "simple" Rails app, which includes the minimum usage of pretty much every feature in Rails in a normal context.

I do not think we need to cover edge cases, but we should have better smoke tests to prevent breakage such as "I can no longer pass `params` to Active Record if I'm using `accepts_nested_attributes_for`

issue.title: AC::Parameters no longer being a Hash has broken find_or_initialize_by
issue.body: Strong parameters can no longer be passed to find_or_initialize_by since it expects a Hash to be passed through to the find_by cal which errors with "Cannot visit ActionController::Parameters.
